summary: Stop repeating historical exec teardown on full reconciliation sweeps once exact-incarnation whole-scope cleanup has been proven and recorded durably.

replay.detail: No graph replay or history backfill. Existing ended execs are checked lazily on reconciliation; unsettled descendants continue to receive native cleanup on later sweeps.

schema.detail: The daemon store adds the node-local local_runtime_cleanup_settled table, keyed by runtime ID and incarnation, with subject ownership and a subject index for reclamation. Installation creates an empty WITHOUT ROWID table and its index; no existing table is scanned, copied, indexed or rewritten, including on stores around 60 GB. No ALTER TABLE migration, observation trigger, shared storage version or client-v0 schema change.

rules.detail: A stopped leader or successful signal is insufficient. Only native exact-generation leader exit plus closed whole-scope proof permits a durable settlement receipt. Missing, unreadable, logical-only or still-populated scopes retain cleanup retries. PTY cleanup is unchanged. Only applying an authoritative, fenced start result reclaims the runtime's superseded receipts in that writer transaction. Late ordinary observations never reclaim receipts. Other retained desired subjects keep their historical receipts, including across projection reconstruction; permanent subject removal reclaims all its receipts in the removal transaction.

compatibility.detail: No client or peer protocol changes. Settlement receipts are local daemon bookkeeping, not replicated claims or graph digests.

downtime.detail: Ordinary daemon restart or rolling deployment. Installation adds an empty table and does not convert historical data; the first sweep may still perform existing historical cleanup work.

manual.detail: No manual migration. Compare historical EndLeftoversLater exec_teardown calls over subsequent full sweeps after rollout; only unsettled or new incarnations should continue teardown.

recovery.detail: Receipts survive daemon and store restart. Older binaries ignore this additive table and safely resume redundant teardown. Losing local settlement receipts restores conservative cleanup work rather than suppressing recovery.
